clue.text: Food arrives, morsel served up with trimmings of lettuce

parts.note: someone who arrives comes

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a bit is a small morsel

indicators.note: trimmings are the edges cut off, so take the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dish turns up with a little garnish of lettuce around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible things in general are called comestibles, a formal synonym for food.

clue.text: See 6
'Rising monetary growth' comprises spin

indicators.note: Rising says the hidden letters are read backwards, upwards in this down clue
the quoted phrase comprises, or contains, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An economist's phrase about rising money supply is dismissed as mere political spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'comprises spin' as the definition, but 'comprises' is the containment signal: the quoted phrase holds ETARYG, which 'Rising' turns upwards. The definition is 'spin' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to whirl round, which is what gyrating means.

clue.text: Dancing around fire pit with a drink

indicators.note: letters dancing around move about, so the fire pit letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Party guests dance round a fire pit, glass in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An apéritif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite.

clue.text: Woman turning bread 8

indicators.note: turning something over or round changes its letter order here
the answer to 8 down says to turn the word inside out, so its middle pair goes to the outside

parts.note: naan is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A woman is turning out bread, perhaps kneading dough.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the cross-reference to INSIDE OUT: NA|AN has its inner AA put outside and its outer Ns put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: The practice of looking after number one?

definitions.text: The practice of looking after number one?

parts.words: The practice of looking after number one?
parts.note: looking after number one usually means selfishness, but number one is also a nursery word for urinating, so this is the medical study of the urinary system

explanation.surface: A sardonic description of selfishness, as if it were a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Urology is the medical specialty dealing with the urinary tract, the bodily side of 'number one'.

clue.text: Turnover-like pud is done unconventionally, adding whiskey

indicators.note: done unconventionally, these letters, with the added W, are put in a new order

parts.note: Whiskey is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A pudding made in an odd way, with a slug of whiskey added.
explanation.walkthrough: The pudding sense is apt: an upside-down cake is turned over after baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned over is inverted, top at the bottom, so it resembles an overturned thing.

clue.text: Being flexible, I'll get drawn into scheme by vacuous celebrity

indicators.note: being drawn into a word means going inside it

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
I'll is read as 'I will', so the I is what is drawn in

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its middle and keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly agreeing to join an empty-headed celebrity's scheme, showing some give.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliancy is the quality of bending easily, so it is the state of being flexible.

clue.text: Studio in west end of Edinburgh revamped thoroughly

indicators.note: revamped means remade, so these letters are reassembled
the west end of a word written across is its left end, its first letter

explanation.surface: A studio in Edinburgh's West End gets a complete makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh's West End is a real district, which disguises the letter selection.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it completely, so the phrase means thoroughly.

clue.text: Yen's calamitous slide returns

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen, and 's stands for has

indicators.note: a calamitous slide is a disastrous one, so its letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A disastrous fall in the yen's value hits investment income.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface suggests 'returns' as income, which is exactly the sense used.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment yields what it returns: both are verbs for producing a profit.

clue.text: Rear 16 birds

indicators.note: 16 across is BACK TO FRONT, so the last letter of the word goes to the front

parts.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Telegraphic: a cross-reference in place of a description of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: Restructure beer co. asap — it's not bloody rocket science!

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds the letters of the brewery phrase in a new order
it's not says one letter must be left out of the restructured pool

parts.note: B is the polite abbreviation for the swear word bloody, as in b***dy

explanation.surface: Telling a brewery to reorganise quickly: it's hardly difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not bloody rocket science' is an idiom for 'it's easy', which hides the definition in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerospace engineering covers rockets and spacecraft, the literal field of rocket science.

clue.text: Put off payment for Trident, supposedly

parts.note: to put off is to deter
rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: Delaying payment for the costly Trident programme, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is Britain's submarine-launched nuclear missile system, and 'supposedly' nods to doubts that it works as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear arms are defended as a deterrent, something that discourages attack.

clue.text: Firm is exciting, humming

parts.note: something that is exciting rocks, in slang
humming is British slang for smelly, and olid means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A company that is thrilling and buzzing with activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' as a business is the false trail; here it is the adjective. 'Humming' is British slang for stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means completely firm and unshakeable.

clue.text: Like a lot of cathedrals and mosques? Tour southern Europe and North Africa, perhaps

definitions.text: Like a lot of cathedrals and mosques?

parts.note: to do a place is to tour it, as in doing Europe
the Med, the Mediterranean region, borders southern Europe and North Africa

explanation.surface: Holiday advice for seeing cathedrals and mosques round the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cathedrals and mosques have a dome, so they are domed buildings.

clue.text: Ran into a sailor, mariner missing bottom part of foot

parts.note: to run into someone is to meet them
a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, here dropped

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced mariner

explanation.surface: A seafaring tale of bumping into an old sea dog lacking a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A metatarsal is one of the long bones in the middle of the foot.

clue.text: Where troops might go after leave's reversed

definitions.text: Where troops might go after leave
definitions.meaning: soldiers on leave go back to the front line when it ends
turned the wrong way round, rear first

explanation.surface: Soldiers' leave has been cancelled, sending them back into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with its rear where its front should be has been turned the wrong way.

clue.text: A beat I incorporated into another from 'South Pacific'?

indicators.note: incorporated into means placed inside another word

parts.note: another beat: to tan someone is to thrash them
to hit is to beat

explanation.surface: A musician adds a beat to a song from the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows 'beat' for a second synonym. The question mark flags that South Pacific is not the musical but the ocean region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia, in the South Pacific, so a native is from there.

clue.text: Hitch, getting lift in northbound vehicle in outlying district

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
in a down clue northbound means travelling upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: getting a lift raises it, upwards in a down clue, so backwards

parts.note: a rub is a hitch or snag, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker gets a lift on a bus heading north to the outskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is a residential area on the edge of a town, an outlying district.

clue.text: Cadge a drink then beat it!

parts.note: to cadge is to beg
one is a drink, as in 'fancy one?'

explanation.surface: A scrounger asks for a drink and is told to get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to go away, as is the slang 'beat it!'.

clue.text: They avail themselves of escorts when hotel's deserted

indicators.note: the letter has deserted, or left, the word

parts.note: ushers escort people to their seats
Hotel is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: Clients making use of escort services once the hotel empties.
explanation.definitionFit: People who avail themselves of something make use of it, so they are its users.

clue.text: Fully covered to make one's destination Italy's Calabria region?

definitions.meaning: covered from top to bottom, completely

definitions.text: to make one's destination Italy's Calabria region?
definitions.meaning: Calabria forms the toe of the boot-shaped Italian peninsula, so travelling there is heading for the toe

explanation.surface: A traveller wrapped up from top to bottom bound for southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed from the top of the head down to the feet means completely covered.

clue.text: Bra in disarray — put in order sharpish

indicators.note: in disarray means jumbled, so the letters of bra are mixed
put in order means the letters of put are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A messy lingerie drawer to be tidied quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means sudden or curt, and sharpish can mean brusque or quick.

clue.text: Cover revolting case of firearm

parts.note: people in revolt are up in arms, or up
a holster is the case a pistol is carried in

explanation.surface: A disgusting gun holster needs a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting but means rebelling, as in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster furniture is to cover it with padding and fabric.

clue.text: 21 seafowl for witches

indicators.note: 21 across is HEAD TO TOE, so the first letter of the word moves to the bottom

parts.note: a shag is a seabird, a kind of cormorant

explanation.surface: A cross-reference turns seabirds into witches.
explanation.definitionFit: Hags are ugly old women, a traditional image of witches.

clue.text: Trunk — character opening it roughly

indicators.note: the character that opens a word is its first letter

parts.note: it refers back to the definition word Trunk
roughly means or so, about

explanation.surface: A trunk's first letter starts the answer, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'Trunk', whose opening character is T.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is the torso.

clue.text: Pour forth out of 6/2 encounter

indicators.note: 6/2 is UPSIDE DOWN, so in this down clue the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to encounter is to meet

explanation.surface: Crowds pour out of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to pour heavily, as rain teems down.

clue.text: Grand plan to broadcast major feature on Bambi?

indicators.note: to broadcast is to speak on air, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Bambi, the Disney fawn, is a deer with big eyes: big eye, deer

explanation.surface: An animator's plan to make a feature film starring Bambi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a film, but means a facial feature: Bambi's big eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A big idea is an ambitious scheme, a grand plan.

clue.text: What cougar will do before assignation

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
an assignation is a date, a romantic meeting

explanation.surface: An older woman seeking a younger man and the date she arranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cougar' also means an older woman pursuing younger men, matching the date surface; the big cat is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cougar is a predator, and to predate is to hunt and prey on animals.
